newsitem.title: USA: US Air has no decision yet about Shuttle.
newsitem.headline: US Air has no decision yet about Shuttle.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc said Thursday it has "exclusive contract rights" to purchase the US Airways Shuttle and is working with the banks that own the commuter air service to determine how to proceed.
American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, said earlier that it signed a binding agreement to buy the Shuttle for an undisclosed price.
American said the deal contingent upon US Airways' decision not to exercise its option to purchase the Shuttle or its right to match American's offer.

The Shuttle is the successor to the former Trump Shuttle. The commuter service was taken over in April 1992 by a group of lenders. US Airways operates the shuttle under a management contract and holds 47 percent of the equity.
In April, US Airways started to assess the value of the Shuttle, but made no decision whether or not it would buy the commuter service.
US Airways' exclusive right to buy the Shuttle ended April 9, but the airline has the right to match any purchase offer made by another party over the next five years.
The Shuttle operates between New York and both Boston and Washington, one of the nation's busiest travel corridors.
